key_insight: Noisy GHZ resources can retain nonclassical correlations and controlled teleportation fidelity above the classical threshold even after genuine multipartite entanglement vanishes.
engineering_relevance: Localizable entanglement may better indicate the operational usefulness of noisy GHZ resources for controlled teleportation in distributed quantum networks.
method: Model bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise using Kraus operators.
Evaluate multipartite discord, genuine multipartite concurrence, localizable entanglement, and controlled teleportation fidelity.
Outline a proof-of-concept photonic GHZ preparation and teleportation implementation.
evidence_signal: The analysis finds broader correlation robustness under bit-flip and amplitude-damping noise, finite-regime discord freezing under bit-flip noise, and above-classical teleportation fidelity after genuine multipartite concurrence vanishes.
watch_item: The photonic implementation is proposed rather than experimentally demonstrated in the abstract, so hardware-level robustness remains unverified.
paper_title: Robustness of Quantum Correlations and Controlled Teleportation Fidelity under Noisy Channels
